mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to increase borrowing and investment, thereby boosting equity markets and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) reflects stronger consumer demand and economic expansion, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by 5% YoY but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 50% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market weakness, which may lead to decreased consumer spending and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.5% in one month
failure_condition: If UNRATE increases by 0.5% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the next 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases and payroll employment (PAYEMS) shows slower growth, it indicates labor market weakness, which should lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If both UNRATE increases and PAYEMS growth slows but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests supply chain constraints or reduced economic activity, which may lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO decreases by 1% MoM but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth (GDPC1) reflects overall economic health. Positive GDP growth should lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: If GDPC1 shows positive growth but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the 60-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) increase borrowing costs and reduce consumer and business spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% in one month
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25% but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the subsequent 20-day periods, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) shows increasing inflation and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is also rising, it indicates tighter monetary conditions, which should lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If both CPIAUCSL increases and FEDFUNDS rises but the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows, the hypothesis is rejected.
